processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Spherical Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni powder (particle diameter 15–53 μm) was PREP-prepared (Advanced Corporation for Materials and Equipments, PREP-22) and used as the SLM feedstock; it is the parent process for the P-110 print.

processing_steps.atmosphere: argon (99.99% pure), oxygen content in forming chamber maintained below 300 ppm
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Printed on an SLM Solutions SLM280 printer; the substrate was heated to 200 °C prior to printing. Laser power 110 W, corresponding to a laser energy density of 91.67 J/mm³. Spot diameter 0.1 mm, layer thickness 0.02 mm, hatch space 0.08 mm, scanning speed 750 mm/s. A 67° rotation angle was applied to each layer with overlapping-strip scanning strategy. Sample denoted P-110.

structures.overall_structure: SLM-printed Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni low-density steel consisting predominantly of γ-Fe(M) austenite with no α-Fe(M) ferrite, containing a small amount of nano-sized κ carbide; transverse cross-section has fine equiaxed grains with random orientation while the longitudinal section is dominated by columnar grains.

phases_present.morphology: fine equiaxed grains with random orientations (different colours in IPF)
phases_present.texture: random orientations, no dominant colour/preferred texture

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: right-skewed distribution with modal bar in lowest few-μm bins, a secondary cluster of bars near 16–20 μm, and bars persisting near 40–44 μm
grain_structure.texture: equiaxed grains with random orientation, no texture

precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix

phases_present.morphology: columnar grains elongated along the vertical build direction extending across deposition-layer boundaries; a small amount of equiaxed grains mainly at the bottom of the melt pool

defects.type: dislocation tangles (high-density, in austenite, from thermal expansion of constituent phases during SLM)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: right-skewed with modal bars near 4–8 μm (about 12–13 % level) and a spread tail out to ~44 μm
grain_structure.texture: columnar grains aligned along the build (vertical) direction

precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix

phase_interfaces.coherence: [011]γ ∥ [011]κ orientation relationship confirmed by SAED and HRTEM

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation tangles / high-density dislocations in austenite
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Dislocation tangles observed inside the austenite owing to thermal expansion of the constituent phases during the SLM process; a region is labelled 'Hight-density dislocation'.

interfaces.phase_evolution: Ferrite formation in the P-110 alloy was suppressed by fast cooling during the SLM process; ferrite diffraction patterns were not detected (printed alloy mainly comprises austenite plus κ carbide).
interfaces.interface_notes: The κ carbide was identified from the selected-area diffraction pattern (zone b) and is uniformly distributed as nanoscale particles in the austenite matrix.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog-bone-shaped tensile sample, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Suns universal testing machine; Reliant electronic extensometer; loading rate 1 mm/min; values also listed in Table 2

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fig. 12: P-110 (blue curve) lies highest over most of the strain range and extends furthest, beyond the 50% gridline

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: microhardness tester at a load of 0.5 kg for 10 s; each value is the arithmetic mean of five measurement points
relative density calculated using the Archimedes principle

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: P-110 yield strength 887.1 MPa, tensile strength 1076.8 MPa, elongation 40.80% vs. as-cast yield strength 772.3 MPa, tensile strength 879.0 MPa, elongation 20.53%; SLM samples show higher strength and plasticity due to rapid cooling-induced grain refinement. P-110 outstanding properties comparable to or even superior to Fe–Mn–Al–C systems prepared by conventional methods.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Bruker D8 Advance X-ray diffractometer, Cu target, continuous scanning, 30–100° 2θ, 2°/min
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification of the SLM-printed P-110 alloy
characterization_methods.key_findings: P-110 mainly comprises the austenite phase (γ-Fe(M)) with no α-Fe(M) phase; FWHM of the (111) peak for P-110 was 0.263.

characterization_methods.technique: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) / inverse pole figure (IPF) mapping
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Oxford Symmetry S2 EBSD instrument (step size 0.3–0.7 μm, accelerating voltage 15–20 kV); data analyzed using TSL OIM software
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize grain morphology, orientation and size
characterization_methods.key_findings: Cross-section of P-110 shows fine equiaxed grains with random orientations; the longitudinal section is dominated by columnar grains elongated along the build direction with a small amount of equiaxed grains at the bottom of the melt pool.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Transverse cross-sections, electrolytically polished in perchloric-acid/ethanol solution
characterization_methods.key_findings: P-110 cross-section almost free of resolvable porosity, printed label 'Porosity=0.13 %', fewest microcracks.

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), SAED, dark-field and HRTEM
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Tecnai F30 scanning transmission electron microscope; TEM samples prepared with a plasma polishing system
characterization_methods.purpose: Study nanoscale κ carbide, dislocations and lattice spacings
characterization_methods.key_findings: Dense dislocation tangles in austenite; κ carbide present (SADP) uniformly distributed as nanoscale particles; [011]γ ∥ [011]κ; HRTEM (200) d=0.262 nm and (1-11) d=0.223 nm; ferrite not detected.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma300 scanning electron microscope; surface roughness measured with a Zeiss LSM 900 laser confocal microscope
characterization_methods.key_findings: P-110 exhibited the best surface quality, devoid of obvious unfused powder particles or pores; a single small sphere labelled 'Balling'; surface roughness Sa = 5.29 μm.

characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) of tensile fracture surfaces
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Post-tensile fracture surfaces, 20 μm scale bar
characterization_methods.key_findings: P-110 shows more-dominant ductile dimple fractures, indicative of superior yield strength, tensile strength and ductility.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Suns universal testing machine with Reliant electronic extensometer
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Dog-bone specimen, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm, loading rate 1 mm/min, room temperature
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure yield strength, tensile strength and elongation
characterization_methods.key_findings: P-110: yield strength 887.1 MPa, tensile strength 1076.8 MPa, elongation 40.80% (highest among SLM samples).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 0.5 kg for 10 s; arithmetic mean of five points; horizontal and vertical cross-sections
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure hardness of cross-sectional and longitudinal sections
characterization_methods.key_findings: P-110 maximum hardness 292 HV (cross-section) and 294 HV (longitudinal section).

unmapped_findings: For the P-110 sample the full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the (111) diffraction peak was 0.263 (XRD).
P-110 surface roughness Sa = 5.29 μm (laser confocal microscopy), the second-lowest of the five SLM samples.
P-110 tensile fracture surface was dominated by ductile dimple rupture (with a higher-magnification dimple inset), consistent with its superior yield strength, tensile strength and ductility.
The P-110 sample was found to have the lowest porosity (0.13%) and fewest microcracks but the highest relative density (99.34%) and maximum density among the SLM-printed samples.
The κ carbide in P-110 was confirmed by SAED dark-field imaging to be composed of nanoscale particles; HRTEM lattice fringes: (200) interplanar spacing 0.262 nm and (1-11) 0.223 nm, zone axis [011].
The outstanding comprehensive mechanical properties of the P-110 sample are comparable to or even superior to those of Fe–Mn–Al–C systems prepared by conventional methods [45–49].

The P-110 sample's lower hardness on the side surface relative to the top surface, and the influence of grain size and internal defects (pores, cracks, unfused powder particles) on hardness, are discussed in the paper.
